newsitem.title: MEXICO: Servant denies multiple killings in Mexico -report.
newsitem.headline: Servant denies multiple killings in Mexico -report.

text.p: A servant who allegedly helped murder a family of five as they slept in their beds earlier this month has claimed to be innocent, news reports said on Wednesday.

Government news agency Notimex said that Alejandro Perez de la Rosa told a court on Tuesday that he did not kill the well-known family, after officials had accused him of the crime that stunned Mexico.
"I did not kill them," Perez was quoted by Notimex as saying.

There had been speculation that the family was murdered in a drug-related hit, or because the parents -- author Yolanda Figueroa and her husband, former anti-drugs agent Fernando Balderas -- had blamed government corruption for delaying the arrest of a top drugs lord.

The Mexico City Attorney General's Office charged on Monday two of the family's chauffeurs had murdered the family in revenge because Balderas had allegedly raped one of their wives and tried to rape the wife of the other. Both women were maids in the household.
Perez had been hospitalized with head injuries after the attack. Police said he confessed to murdering the family with the help of his fellow driver and the two wives.

In a book published in August, Figueroa alleged that the government had all the elements it needed to capture jailed cocaine kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego nearly three years before his arrest in January 1996 -- raising speculation that drugs or politics may have been the motive for the family's murder.
Her book relied largely on information from Balderas, who was a key adviser in the attorney general's office in the early 1990s.
